question: How do I export a YOLO model to TensorRT with INT8 quantization?
reference: Export with format='engine' and quantize=8 (it replaces the deprecated int8/half flags) and pass a dataset YAML with data= for calibration, for example model.export(format='engine', dynamic=True, batch=8, workspace=4, quantize=8, data='coco.yaml').

question: Why should INT8 calibration be done on the same device that will run the model?
reference: INT8 calibration results vary across devices, so the device that will run the TensorRT engine should be the one used for the INT8 export; calibrating on a borrowed high-end GPU can give poor performance on another device.

question: What does the workspace argument control in TensorRT export, and what should I do if calibration crashes?
reference: workspace sets the maximum workspace size in GiB that TensorRT may use while optimizing and converting the model; the default None lets TensorRT allocate automatically. If calibration crashes, set workspace=None or reduce imgsz and batch. If workspace is larger than the device memory, TensorRT reports UNSUPPORTED_STATE and the value must be lowered.

question: Which tracker does model.track use if I don't pass a tracker argument?
reference: TrackTrack (tracktrack.yaml) is the default tracker.

question: Which tracker should I pick for drone or other moving-camera footage?
reference: BoT-SORT, because it adds camera-motion compensation and optional ReID.

question: How do I keep the same object IDs across frames when I call the tracker on each frame of a video in a loop?
reference: Pass persist=True to model.track(). It tells the tracker that the frame is the next one in the same sequence, so it reuses state from earlier frames and keeps track IDs consistent. It should not be used across unrelated images or a different stream.

question: How can I avoid running out of memory when running inference on a very long video?
reference: Use stream=True so inference returns a generator of Results objects that keeps only the current frame's results in memory, instead of the default list holding results for every frame.

question: How do I resume a training run that was interrupted?
reference: Call train with resume=True on the partially trained .pt checkpoint (for example last.pt). Training restores the weights, optimizer state, learning-rate scheduler, epoch number and dataset and continues where it stopped.

question: Can I train on multiple GPUs on Windows?
reference: No. Multi-GPU training does not work on Windows with the official PyTorch wheels for torch>=2.4, because the DDP rendezvous needs libuv, which those wheels lack, and USE_LIBUV=0 does not help. Train on Linux or WSL2 with device=[0, 1], or use a single GPU with device=0 on Windows.

question: What is the difference between mAP50 and mAP50-95?
reference: mAP50 is mean average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.50, so it only measures the easier detections. mAP50-95 averages mAP over IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, which gives a fuller view of performance across localization difficulty.

question: How does model.tune search for good hyperparameters?
reference: It uses a genetic algorithm: it mutates the hyperparameters of the best results so far, trains with them, and keeps the settings that maximize fitness over the iterations.

question: Which export format gives the fastest inference on a Raspberry Pi?
reference: NCNN, because it is highly optimized for mobile and embedded ARM platforms.

question: How do I run a YOLO model on the Jetson DLA cores?
reference: Export to TensorRT with device='dla:0' (or 'dla:1') and FP16 or INT8 precision, for example model.export(format='engine', device='dla:0', quantize=16). DLA only works with FP16 or INT8, and TensorRT 10.7 is the last TensorRT release with DLA support.

question: Is it safe to share one YOLO model object between several Python threads?
reference: No. Sharing one instance causes race conditions that corrupt its internal state. Create a separate YOLO model inside each thread, or use the ThreadingLocked decorator.

question: How can I detect small objects in very high-resolution images?
reference: Use SAHI sliced inference: the image is split into overlapping slices (for example slice_height=256, slice_width=256, overlap ratio 0.2), detection runs on each slice, and the results are merged.

question: How do I count people crossing a line in a video?
reference: Use the ObjectCounter solution with a region: two points define a line, and three or more define a polygon. It tracks each object across frames and counts IN and OUT crossings.

question: How does the speed estimation solution turn pixel movement into a real-world speed?
reference: SpeedEstimator tracks each object across frames and converts its pixel displacement into speed using the video frame rate (fps) and a real-world scale, meter_per_pixel, which you tune to your camera setup.

question: How do I benchmark a YOLO model across all export formats?
reference: Use benchmark from ultralytics.utils.benchmarks, for example benchmark(model='yolo26n.pt', data='coco8.yaml', imgsz=640, device=0), or the yolo benchmark CLI. Leaving format blank tests every supported format; format='onnx' tests only that one.

question: How much faster can OpenVINO make inference on Intel CPUs?
reference: Exporting to OpenVINO can give up to a 3x CPU speedup, and also enables acceleration on Intel GPUs and NPUs.

question: Does YOLO26 still need non-maximum suppression?
reference: YOLO26 trains a one-to-many head and a one-to-one head. By default prediction and validation use the one-to-many head with NMS, which favors accuracy; setting nms=False uses the faster NMS-free one-to-one head.

question: How do I deploy YOLO with NVIDIA DeepStream on a Jetson?
reference: Use the marcoslucianops/DeepStream-Yolo repository: clone it, export the YOLO model to ONNX, copy the .onnx model and labels.txt into the DeepStream-Yolo folder, configure it, and run it with DeepStream.

question: What do I need to set up to serve a YOLO model with Triton Inference Server?
reference: Export the model to ONNX, build a Triton model repository containing the model and a config.pbtxt (with the model metadata added), then start the Triton Inference Server pointing at that repository.
